 Order
This is first bail application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 438 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of anticipatory bail.

2 . Applicant apprehending her arrest in connection with Crime No.20 of 2025 registered at P.S.-
Kevlari, District-Seoni (M.P) for the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471/ 34 of the IPC for grant of anticipatory bail.

3. Prosecution story in brief is that applicant as well as other persons were owner of Survey No.431,
436/1 and 438/1 and on 21.12.2013, 0.44 hectare land and it was acquired by the Railway and compensation was also paid but still, on 13.02.2015, applicant sold above aforesaid land through power of attorney executed in favour of his brother in lieu of Rs.2,18,000/- to the complainant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that at the time of execution of power of attorney in favour of her brother, applicant was not aware that land has already been acquired by the Railways.
It is also urged that there was no entry in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12429 2 MCRC-11328-2025 the name of Railway after acquisition.
Allegedly, land was acquired on 21.12.2013, power of attorney was executed on 04.02.2015 and sale deed has been executed on 13.02.2015.

Applicant is ready to deposit the sale Smt. Jyoti Janghela vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24658256/
1 consideration i.e. Rs.2,18,000/-.

entities.text: Smt. Jyoti Janghela vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On above grounds, it is urged that applicant be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
5 . Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
6. Looking to overall facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it proper to release the applicant on anticipatory bail.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest, subject to depositing of sum Rs.2,18,000/- before the trial Court the applicant shall be released on bail on her executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer/Investigating Authority.

8. The applicant shall further abide by other conditions enumerated under Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and shall cooperate in the investigation otherwise this bail order shall automatically stand cancelled.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Smt. Jyoti Janghela vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24658256/
